mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the previous three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous increase in the housing starts index (HOUST), signals an expansion in both manufacturing and construction, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA and HOUST > 12-mo MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000, combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a rapidly tightening labor market, which raises wage inflation and cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 and UNRATE falls by >0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS > 200000 and UNRATE falls by >0.2pp in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month average, coupled with a flat or rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL), signals that households are drawing down savings to maintain consumption, which increases borrowing costs and reduces future consumption growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-mo MA for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL >= 12-mo MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative under the specified RSAFS and CPIAUCSL conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is held constant for three consecutive months after a prior tightening cycle, market expectations of prolonged low rates support equity valuations via lower discount rates, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged for three consecutive months after a prior rate hike cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is unchanged for three months after a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction-related earnings and broader economic activity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-mo MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months.
